column21: Description: Sukajadi (Sukajadi Pasar) is a shell midden site in northern Sumatra, part of the Bukit Kerang tradition. The site contains evidence of early Holocene occupation with marine shell deposits and is associated with early Homo sapiens in the region. Similar to other Bukit Kerang sites in Aceh Tamiang.

column21: Description: Tamiang (Bukit Kerang) is a shell midden site in Aceh Tamiang Regency, Aceh. The site is part of the widespread Bukit Kerang tradition of prehistoric hunter-gatherer sites in northern Sumatra, dating to the Holocene period. Shell deposits indicate marine resource exploitation by early coastal communities.

column21: Description: This shell mound is approximately 4.5 meters high, 20 meters wide, and 25 meters long. The site area is 36 x 31 square meters. Several excavations and research activities conducted by the Medan Archaeological Center have uncovered various types of stone tools, human and animal bone fragments, animal teeth, human teeth, and rock fragments. These findings support the hypothesis that this area was once used for residential purposes.

column21: Description: This site is a collection of mussel or shell waste that has accumulated into a mound. The hill consists of several mounds that merge to form a hill with a length of about 94 meters and a height of 4 meters from the surrounding ground. Initially, it was widely dug by local residents for lime raw material, so that on the northern side the first mound appears damaged. This first mound has an area of about 2200 m2 with details of 48 meters long and 46 meters wide.

column21: Description: This cave site is about 25 m long and 5 to 7 m wide. The cave entrance is 2 meters high with a diameter of 1.6 meters. There are stalactites and stalagmites, some of which are shaped like statues associated with the Legend of Putri Pukes. There is also a well in the middle of the cave room. The well has a diameter of 4 m and a depth of 2 meters. In addition, there is a stone mortar, a grinding stone, and pottery fragments, one of each. Additionally, several stone tools from the Neolithic period and microliths were also found.
